fixes.explanation: Paul says to "…strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God." Notice the target is the things above, with Christ right there. It isn't a goal you'd put on a poster. I think that's a great thing to aim at, friend.

That's a fair guess, but it isn't what verse 1 says. Paul says to strive for "…the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God." He starts from the fact that they've been raised with Christ, so his aim is the things above, not a rulebook. I think that's good news, friend.
Paul writes, "For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God." Hidden with Christ, tucked in God like a batch tucked in the oven. That's a lot packed into one sentence.
Moses is a big name, and I get why he came to mind. But Paul says their life is "…hidden with Christ in God." Moses isn't in this verse at all. Christ is the one their life is hidden with.

Abraham is a famous name, so no shame in reaching for him. Still, Paul says their life is "…hidden with Christ in God." Abraham doesn't make an appearance in this verse. It's Christ, baker, every time.

Paul says the opposite. He writes, "When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways." He's talking to the Colossians about their own past, and he doesn't sugarcoat it. I think that's a kindness.

Pride and envy didn't make this list, friend. Paul names "anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips." Those two feel like they belong in the crowd, and I get why they came to mind. But verse 8 never invites them.

Laziness and grumbling? Not in verse 8, baker. Paul's list is "anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips." I'll admit I've done plenty of grumbling over a hot oven, but Paul didn't put it here.

Right, it's false. Paul tells them to "…forgive any complaint you may have against someone else." He doesn't add a condition. Then he gives the measure: "Forgive as the Lord forgave you." Any complaint, baker, so no leftovers.

Faith is a good one, but it's not the word in this verse. Paul says to put on "…love, which is the bond of perfect unity." Love is the piece that goes over all the rest. In this verse, love is the one called the bond of perfect unity.

Paul says, "Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom…" The word dwells in them, and it spills out as they teach and admonish each other. Admonish is a word for warning and advising. Good one, baker.
